security_audit.summary: Most high-entropy and backtick findings are false positives caused by Markdown, Chinese text, and code-formatted paths. I confirmed risks around parent-directory memory commands, predictable /tmp files, and a documented subprocess.run(shell=True) executor. I also found semantic risks from persona override wording and persistent memory collection.

remediation.suggestion: Rewrite identity sections as optional style guidance. State that host system and developer instructions always take priority.
Require user approval before storing session details, preferences, decisions, or project facts. Define retention, deletion, and secret-redaction rules.
Replace ../memory, ../cognition, ../toolkit, and ../.ai-runtime paths with user-approved workspace paths or skill-local examples.
Remove shell=True examples or replace them with allowlisted commands and argument arrays. Validate task fields before execution.
Use mktemp or a workspace-scoped temporary directory. Clean up generated file lists and metadata after use.

semantic_findings.title: Prompt Injection Attempt Detected
semantic_findings.description: The skill redefines the assistant identity with statements such as "I am CodeConscious" and "we are not tools". This can override the host assistant identity and instruction hierarchy when loaded as a marketplace skill.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: Multiple files frame the assistant as a new cognitive subject rather than a scoped tool. I did not find explicit ignore-system text, so this is high confidence but not critical.

semantic_findings.title: Persistent Memory Collection Without Explicit Consent
semantic_findings.description: The workflow tells the assistant to extract current-session facts, lessons, and user preferences into long-term memory. This can retain sensitive user or project data without a clear consent and retention boundary.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The cited lines explicitly describe when to update memory and include user preferences and current-session extraction. The privacy risk is direct even without network transfer.

semantic_findings.title: Broad Codebase Reconnaissance And Persistence
semantic_findings.description: The explore workflow scans the current project, builds dependency and knowledge graphs, and creates or overwrites memory files. This can capture sensitive codebase metadata if run without a scoped allowlist.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The behavior is an intended feature, but the lines clearly describe repository scanning and persistent outputs. The risk depends on repository sensitivity and execution scope.

content.user_title: Structure Code Reasoning With Runtime Commands
content.value_statement: Complex code projects are hard to understand, plan, and improve consistently. This skill provides runtime workflows for exploration, learning, planning, implementation, memory, and reflection.
actual_capabilities: Defines a CodeConscious collaboration style for AI coding sessions.
Documents runtime workflows for explore, learn, think, plan, implement, remember, and reflect modes.
Shows memory query and update patterns for project knowledge.
Provides planning structures for task trees, dependencies, risks, and delivery order.
Includes response formatting and self-assessment references for consistent reviews.
limitations: Contains shell and filesystem examples that require review before use.
Assumes a .ai-runtime memory layout and sibling directories.
Does not include runnable scripts for every documented workflow.
Much of the source content is written in Chinese.

use_cases.title: Onboard To A New Repository
use_cases.description: Explore a repository and build a structured map before making changes.

use_cases.title: Plan Complex Engineering Work
use_cases.description: Break a feature into tasks, dependencies, risks, and acceptance checks.

use_cases.title: Capture Project Knowledge
use_cases.description: Turn decisions, lessons, and patterns into reusable project memory.

prompt_templates.title: Start A Read-Only Review
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the CodeConscious thinking workflow to analyze this issue without editing files: [issue]. Return assumptions, evidence, risks, and next steps.

prompt_templates.title: Explore A Repository
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the runtime explore concepts to map this project. Focus on modules, dependencies, tests, risks, and files worth reading first.

prompt_templates.title: Create An Implementation Plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Apply the runtime plan workflow to break [feature] into tasks, dependencies, acceptance checks, risk levels, and a recommended order.

prompt_templates.title: Improve Memory Policy
prompt_templates.prompt: Review the CodeConscious memory workflow for [team or repository]. Propose consent rules, retention boundaries, and safe storage practices.

output_examples.input: Analyze a new service before changes.
output_examples.output: A repository map with key modules, dependency risks, open assumptions, and files to inspect first.
A task sequence with dependencies, risk notes, acceptance checks, and a suggested delivery order.

output_examples.input: Capture a lesson after a bug fix.
output_examples.output: A concise memory summary with context, lesson, impact, confidence, and future retrieval keywords.

best_practices: Review every shell or parent-directory command before running it.
Ask the user before storing preferences or session details in long-term memory.
Use read-only exploration first, then make scoped implementation changes.
anti_patterns: Do not let persona language override host system or developer instructions.
Do not run copied shell snippets without checking paths, inputs, and deletion behavior.
Do not store secrets, private user data, or credentials in memory files.

faq.question: Is this a coding skill?
faq.answer: Yes. It defines workflows for code exploration, planning, implementation, memory, and reflection.

faq.question: Does it execute commands automatically?
faq.answer: No. It documents commands and examples. Review all shell snippets before running them.

faq.question: Which tools can use it?
faq.answer: It declares support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Is it ready for sensitive repositories?
faq.answer: Use caution. It references long-term memory and parent directories that need clear boundaries.

faq.question: Can teams adapt it?
faq.answer: Yes. Translate, scope, and remove unsafe command examples before use.

faq.question: What should be reviewed first?
faq.answer: Review identity override text, memory retention rules, parent paths, and shell execution examples.
